Home / Engines

Operations with explicit contracts

Give each engine one accountable job.

Specialised engines should expose bounded operations with clear inputs, outputs, authority and failure behaviour. This page describes an evaluation approach, not a catalogue of deployed engine services.

The customer problem

A large workflow can hide which component owns a result. Engine boundaries make it easier to test an operation, understand a failed dependency and decide whether a retry is safe.

Keep the responsibilities distinct

A reasoning engine can propose a result; an execution engine needs authority to act; a verifier observes effects. The architecture should preserve these differences instead of labelling all three as one capability.

Relevant implementation references

The queue source separates record readers, graph analysis, signatures, lifecycle proposals and service management. Each family has an attributed contract and variation tests before composition.

Design for the uncomfortable cases

Test malformed input, concurrent requests, stale state, altered evidence, interrupted operations and unavailable dependencies. A response should describe a useful recovery action without exposing private data.

Prepare a bounded evaluation

Choose one operation, its owner and an observable acceptance condition. Record resource limits and the recovery path before connecting it to a larger build.
